svg.title: The seat record's fields and who reads them, and which identity carries the start time
svg.text: One record, three readers, and the identity that owns the start time
seat record — watch_lock_path(project)
pid · pid_start_time · host — which process wrote it
started_at — when that process took the seat
reckon_version — names the install
code_stamp — the code this producer runs
The version holds still across the commits a
reader needs to see; only the stamp moves. So
a seat is current by version and stale by code,
and nothing told the two apart.
the cursor's producer key — read by nothing: its consumer takes stream_path and baseline
the live view — code_stamp and code_stale, for any Python caller and the MCP read
the follower's attach line — one dim line, and the command that cycles the seat
started_at travels only across this producer's own image replacement
a dead predecessor's record, never erased
pid 999912 · pid_start_time 1.0 · host this host
Carried from whatever sits in the file, this
becomes the fresh producer's start time: armed
a second ago, read as though up for hours.
this process, arriving at the same file
pid · pid_start_time · host of this process,
compared against the record's own three
All three equal — a replacement of this
producer, so its start time is kept.
Any of them different — an arming, stamps now.
